chapter: Bill Robinson and Chuck and Chuckles
title: Robinson's influence and his numbered tap steps
summary: Green says Robinson and Bubbles had the greatest influence; Robinson numbered his steps, even and manly, and Green demonstrates what Robinson taught him.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yes. Definitely. Yeah, he had the greatest influence, he and John Bubbles, you see, of Buck and Bubbles. See, because Jack Wiggins was not -- I think he was unknown up here at that time. He used to travel on the TOBA, and that was mostly in the south, you know. And therefore, Bill Bojangles Robinson was making tap dancing recognizable when people would -- when they'd speak of tap dancing, they'd speak of it like they speak of ballet, you see. Because there was a lot of different works in tap dancing, see? You had what they called the unison tap. They had precision tap

dancing. They had novelty tap dancing, you see. And they had trick tap dancing. His tap dancing consisted of steps. And that was tap dancing. Because he would always say -- he had a routine where he would say, "Number one tap step." And when he would demonstrate the number one tap step. But it was fascinating. As I say, they all would do some kind of buck. See? And he had a way of doing the time step, and he called that number one step, you see?
Was his way of doing the time step different from other dancers' ways of doing the time step?
What would he do, he'd go up on his toes more?

Yes. Yes. He was very masculine, see. He was manly about it. He Looked So refreshing, you know. Just like watching big drops of rain coming down, he was so even. Well, he really was ambidextrous. Anything that he could do on one foot, he could do on the other. Both feet he could do. Then he could do some of the steps with both feet at the same time, and that's how this dance, this tap dance he called number one step, number two step, number three step, number four step, number five step, and that's the tap dance routine, see?
Can you do some of that Bill Robinson stuff?
Yeah, well I can do what he taught me.
I'd like to hear that one again. (Recording interruption)
